title: Core Blockly Components
description: Understand the fundamental Blockly components used to build algorithms visually inside AlgoBlocks.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
AlgoBlocks uses Blockly components to help students build algorithms through visual programming.

Each block represents a programming instruction or logical operation. By combining blocks together, learners can create complete algorithms without immediately dealing with programming syntax.

Understanding the purpose of each component is important because these blocks form the foundation of all future algorithm activities.

sections.title: Variables
sections.content:
Variables are used to store information temporarily while an algorithm executes.

A variable can hold numbers, text, or other forms of data that may change during execution.

Programmers use variables to track values, store calculations, and manage the state of an algorithm while it runs.

sections.title: Loops
sections.content:
Loops allow algorithms to repeat instructions multiple times automatically.

Instead of manually writing the same instructions repeatedly, programmers use loops to perform repetitive tasks efficiently.

Loops are extremely important in programming because many real-world problems require repeated processing of data, calculations, or user actions.

sections.title: Conditional Logic
sections.content:
Conditional logic allows algorithms to make decisions.

Using if and else conditions, the program can choose different actions depending on whether a condition is true or false.

Decision-making is a core part of programming because algorithms often need to react differently depending on the situation.

sections.title: Arrays
sections.content:
Arrays are used to store multiple related values inside a single structure.

Instead of creating many separate variables, programmers use arrays to organize collections of data efficiently.

Arrays are commonly used for managing lists, processing datasets, and performing algorithm operations such as searching and sorting.

sections.title: Math Operations in Algorithms
sections.content:
Algorithms frequently perform mathematical operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, and comparison.

These operations are used in calculations, scoring systems, simulations, data analysis, and many other computational tasks.

Understanding how mathematical blocks work is essential because mathematics forms the foundation of many computer science concepts.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
sections.content: Blockly components allow students to build algorithms visually using variables, loops, conditions, arrays, and mathematical operations. These components form the foundation of algorithm design and problem-solving inside AlgoBlocks.
